findings.claim: "The multiplier this stage is named for was live in 35 games, not 68; in 85 of 120 it never appeared and the deck still took its 27 wins, 20 with Approach."
findings.note: MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE, and this is the number the whole conversion-stage argument turns on. Cross-tabbing the run record's own per-game fields — games[].per_seat.heliod.commander_transformed_turn against games[].winner and games[].won_by, in sim/giada-angels-vs-baylen-tokens-vs-abaddon-n120-996adb84-s573917060-podExperimental-c600.json — gives: 85 games with NO transform hold 23 wins and 18 Approach wins; 35 games WITH transform hold 4 wins and 2 Approach wins. So it is 23 of the 27 and 18 of the 20, not all of them. REBUT BY STRENGTHENING, NOT WEAKENING: the corrected split makes the point harder, since the no-flip win rate is 23/85 = 0.271 against 4/35 = 0.114 with the flip, and the commander never RESOLVED at all in the games holding 17 of the 27 wins (games_resolved 68 hold only 10). Do not assert causation from that — long games are both the ones you flip in and the ones you lose — but the artifact currently claims a clean 27/85 that the record does not contain. A `commander_transformed_turn` x `winner` cross-tab is one pass over games[] and could be a permanent check on any line that prices a commander event against a win column.

findings.claim: "Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain and Loran are the four gift pieces that feed the discount on your own turn."
findings.note: A closed-set claim, presented as the correction that motivated re-pointing the line, and the set is larger than four. Swept every oracle_text in the 99 for text that makes an opponent draw. INSIDE the ignition stage the model missed two: The Second Doctor — "How Civil of You — At the beginning of YOUR end step, each player may draw a card" — and Forced Fruition — "Whenever an opponent casts a spell, that player draws seven cards", which fires whenever an opponent casts an instant during your turn, for {7}. That is six, not four. OUTSIDE the stage there are more: Scrawling Crawler "At the beginning of YOUR upkeep, each player draws a card" (free, automatic, every turn, and placed in `output`), Faerie Mastermind "{3}{U}: Each player draws a card" (in `conversion`), and Skyscribing's forecast "{2}{U}, Reveal this card from your hand: Each player draws a card. (Activate only during your upkeep...)" (in `fuel`). The artifact already contradicts itself here: stages[2].what_it_does says Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius and Mathemagics "feed the same turn's discount only when aimed at an opponent". The Second Doctor omission is the costly one — its window is your own end step, which is exactly the window open_questions[2] asks about for the second Approach under the flash grant. The NEGATIVE half of the note (Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami, Dictate fire in each player's draw step and contribute {0} on your turn) is correct and should be kept verbatim.

findings.claim: "Drop Pearl Medallion and Sapphire Medallion from the any_of" ... "two of its eight members cannot contribute to the event the label is about" ... "a 0.823 assembled_rate for this target"
findings.note: MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE. The proposal is void: goldfish_targets.json's "Heliod plus the mana to flip him" any_of holds SIX members — Arcane Signet, Azorius Signet, Decanter of Endless Water, Sol Ring, Talisman of Progress, Thought Vessel — and `grep -c Medallion goldfish_targets.json` returns 0. Git shows why: the Medallions were in that any_of through 7aa3d17 and were removed at c879dcd, the same commit that shipped this engine.json, so the proposal describes a file state that no longer exists. The rate is stale from the same moment — 0.823 is 7aa3d17's goldfish_metrics figure for that target; the current file reads assembled_rate 0.732, by_turn_6 0.554, mean_turn 4.852. This also falsifies notes[4], which states the proposals "were verified against goldfish_targets.json before this one was written". The RULES point inside the proposal is sound and worth keeping somewhere — a cost reduction on spells cannot pay any part of "{3}{U/P}: Transform Heliod", an activated ability — but it is now a fact about a fix already made, not a pending edit. A check that every card named in a proposed_goldfish_edits target actually appears in that target is cheap and general.

findings.claim: "Pearl Medallion and Sapphire Medallion ... In this deck they do the rocks' job — shave the bill on a colour-heavy curve — which is also how goldfish_targets counts them."
findings.note: MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE. goldfish_targets.json does not count them at all: neither Medallion appears in any of the eleven targets' `need` groups (zero occurrences of the string "Medallion" in the file). Same root cause as the finding on proposed_goldfish_edits[0] — both sentences were written against the pre-c879dcd target list. The cross-reference in stages[0].what_it_does ("and why they cannot pay any part of the commander's flip; see proposed_goldfish_edits") points at the same void proposal and needs to go with it.

findings.claim: "benchmark response: answer_cards 21, answer_share 0.25, 6 of 15 classes covered; the 5 remaining cards in this stage (the three taxers and two Wall-type blockers) carry no answer role at all"
findings.note: MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE. Re-derived over card_roles.json using benchmark.json's own six classes (counterspell, protection:self, removal:bounce, removal:damage, removal:spot, removal:sweeper): SIX cards in the protection stage carry no answer role — Propaganda, Ghostly Prison, Archangel of Tithes, Angelic Wall, Drift of Phantasms, and LEYLINE OF ANTICIPATION, which the same stage's own prose lists under COMMANDER INSURANCE and which deck-facts puts in `roles.no_role`. The "5" is 26 minus 21, which silently assumes all 21 answer cards sit in this stage. They do not: Walking Ballista carries `removal:damage` and is the deck's only card in that class, and this model files it in `output`. So the arithmetic is 26 − 20 = 6. The gap is itself worth naming — benchmark counts Walking Ballista among the 21 answers while the engine model reads it as output, which is a real disagreement between two artifacts about one card and is not currently in map_disagreements. The three benchmark headline figures (21 / 0.25 / 6 of 15) are exact and should be kept.

findings.claim: "`eliminated_by` attributes 39 of heliod's 53 ATTRIBUTED eliminations to giada-angels, whose every threat flies."
findings.note: The enumeration was not run and it has two exceptions. Enumerated data/opponents/giada-angels/decklist.txt against the corpus: 31 creature cards plus the commander Giada, Font of Hope = 32, of which THIRTY carry the flying keyword. The two that do not are Starnheim Aspirant (Creature — Human Cleric, "Angel spells you cast cost {2} less to cast") and BISHOP OF WINGS (Creature — Human Cleric), whose only occurrence of the word flying is on the Spirit tokens it makes when an Angel dies — the exact text-match trap CLAUDE.md warns about. strategic_frame.json makes the same claim as "31 of whose 32 creature cards carry flying ... the lone exception is Starnheim Aspirant" and misses Bishop of Wings too, so an unenumerated figure has now been copied forward and HARDENED into an unqualified superlative. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES — 30 of 32, and both exceptions are two-power support bodies, so reading the 39 eliminations as coming from the air is well carried — but the phrase as written is false, and it is the stated justification for v1.2.0's fort layer and for the label on goldfish_targets' flier-blocker target ("39 of 53 eliminations came from the air"). Re-scope to what survived rather than dropping the argument.

findings.claim: "the checker's own audit says the game_history sentence 'is scenario flavor per orchestrator instruction, NOT A RULES CLAIM'"
findings.note: The quote is real but its scope has been widened. Stack 002's checker audit reads: "The 'Last night's end step' phrase in game_history is scenario flavor per orchestrator instruction, not a rules claim." The checker scoped that to one phrase — a timing detail — not to the whole game_history sentence and not to the Mystical Tutor premise. THE VERDICT IS CORRECT AND MUST STAND: Mystical Tutor appears only in scenario.graveyard and scenario.extras.game_history, no resolution step reasons about it, and stack 002 therefore does not prove fuel → wincon. Downgrading this line was the right call and this finding is about the quote, not the decision. Replace with the checker's exact sentence and rest the downgrade on the resolution steps, which carry it on their own.

findings.claim: "The declared 'Engine + punisher assembled' component prices the two-piece at 0.328 assembled, 0.196 by turn six"
findings.note: No component with that label exists in goldfish_targets.json or goldfish_metrics.json. The live label is "Table draw engine plus a draw-triggered drain, both drawn". A check that a quoted component label matches a goldfish_targets label is mechanical.

findings.claim: "engine-critic re-derived the same logs and got several times that from those three cards alone, an open attribution question about the parser."
findings.note: The CLAIM IS TRUE — I re-derived it independently — but the citation form is unusable: it cites an agent by name, engine.json carries no `critic` key at all, and the only copy of that agent's output lives in gitignored .agent-out/, so no reader can check it. Cite the derivation instead of the byline. From the run's own logs (sim/logs/.../part-0*.log), counting `Resolve Stack: <card>` lines: Iron Maiden 26, Viseling 33, Ebony Owl Netsuke 22 = 81, which confirms the artifact's "81 castings ... (26 + 33 + 22)" EXACTLY. Summing `Damage: <card> (id) deals N non-combat damage to <seat>` over the same logs, excluding lines aimed at an mm-heliod seat: 1,002 points across 120 games, mean 8.35 a game, against the record's seat figure noncombat_damage_dealt_to_players.mean of 1.68 — a factor of 5.0. findings.claim: "Approach of the Second Sun", asserted in the field with no qualifier
findings.note: Low severity and the prose is honest, but the field is machine-read and the caveat that carries it lives only in what_it_does: the same stage says "roughly a quarter of the wins did not need the card", and I confirm 7 of heliod's 27 wins read won_by "all opponents have lost" (20 read the Approach effect — an exact match to the artifact's tally). deck_audit's own `engine.single_points_of_failure` is `[]`, since every declared component has two or more members; this model asserts one and does not note the disagreement. It is a defensible authored SPOF — the stage genuinely holds one card and there is no second finisher — but a consumer reading the field alone gets an unqualified claim about a deck that closes without it a quarter of the time.

Not a content finding; a revision-feasibility one, raised because three of the findings above land in stages that have no room. Measured lengths: conversion 1797, mana 1784, output 1783, protection 1774, ignition 1644, wincon 1690, fuel 1545. Four of seven sit within 30 characters of the cap and conversion has THREE. The conversion correction (23/27 and 18/20 rather than 27 and 20) and the protection correction (six roleless cards, not five; the Bishop of Wings exception) cannot be written without cutting existing text first. Nothing here is muddled — the prose is dense but each paragraph does one job — so the cut should come from the figures that are restated elsewhere, not from the reasoning.

findings.claim: the three closed-set enumerations: only two cards can find Approach; four cards lift the discard step; Enlightened Tutor reaches five of the ten gift pieces
findings.note: All three swept over the 85 entries and all three are right. "Search your library" appears on exactly five cards — Mystical Tutor (instant or sorcery), Long-Term Plans (any card), Enlightened Tutor (artifact or enchantment), Drift of Phantasms (transmute at mana value 3 against Approach's 7) and Flooded Strand (a Plains or Island) — so only the first two can reach a {6}{W} Sorcery, and Dig Through Time is a look, not a search. "maximum hand size" appears on exactly four — Reliquary Tower, Decanter of Endless Water and Thought Vessel read "You", The Second Doctor reads "Players" — so the asymmetry the output stage prices is real. Enlightened Tutor reaches exactly Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Temple Bell (Artifacts), Dictate of Kruphix and Forced Fruition (Enchantments) among the ten; Kami, Mikokoro, Kwain, Loran and The Second Doctor are out on type. The X-spell partition is also correct: nine cards carry {X}, five draw (two symmetric — Prosperity, Skyscribing — and three targeted), four leave a permanent. lines[1] and lines[6] check out on the rules as well: Font of Mythos adds 6 opponent draws a cycle for 12 Sphinx cards and 9 draws for 18 in total (CR 121.2, each card is a separate draw event), and Alhammarret's Archive replaces both of Sphinx's draws when they happen outside your own draw step, for four (CR 614.5 stops re-application), so "four cards, not two" holds.

findings.claim: "that decomposition is not on disk in this deck's artifacts and is repeated here as the version's stated rationale, not as a figure I re-derived"
findings.note: Independently confirmed and it is the best-behaved sentence in the artifact. deck_versions.json v1.1.0 does say "a 45% removal rate" and "the decomposition of 119 measured departures" — quoted exactly — and searching every JSON under data/decks/heliod/ for the decomposition itself (mass/targeted split, exile share, the 173 denominator) returns nothing. diagnosis.json reaches the same conclusion independently: "The commander-removal decomposition that justified v1.1.0 ... is NOT ON DISK in this deck's artifacts. engine.json says so explicitly and repeats it as the version's claim rather than as a measurement." Two artifacts agreeing that a figure is missing is the right shape for an unmeasurable claim. lines[5] is the same discipline done well — the X-cost interaction is left as a claim with open_questions[0] carrying it, rather than settled from memory.

critic.note: Round 1, and the first time this model has been criticised. The engineer was re-run on 2026-09-03 with an earlier critique's findings and the result was never put back in front of the critic, so a document that answered a critique carried no verdict saying it had. Five of sixteen findings are `supported`; the rest are corrections, and the largest of them STRENGTHENS the model rather than weakening it — the deck wins 23 of 85 games where Heliod never flips (0.271) against 4 of 35 where he does (0.114), re-derived independently from giada-angels-vs-baylen-tokens-vs-abaddon-n120-996adb84 and matching the critic exactly. NOT cache-recorded: a fail model documents what could not be grounded.

lines.note: RE-POINTED, and the reason is a trap worth naming. Mikokoro's "{2}, {T}: Each player draws a card" fires on YOUR turn, so three opponents drawing one apiece is {3} off the next spell you cast that turn under "cost {1} less for each card your opponents have drawn THIS TURN". Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon and Dictate of Kruphix cannot do this: they fire "at the beginning of each player's draw step", and an opponent's draw step falls on that opponent's own turn, so on your turn they contribute {0}. Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain and Loran are the four gift pieces that feed the discount on your own turn. Gated on the BACK face, which appeared in 0.292 of Forge games, and not modelled by the goldfish - model-coverage gives Heliod only the bodies channel - so every mana figure in this artifact is a floor. Claim, not fact.
via: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

lines.note: Font of Mythos is "at the beginning of each player's draw step, that player draws TWO ADDITIONAL cards", so it ADDS six opponent draws a round cycle - twelve extra cards for you through Consecrated Sphinx, which draws two on every opponent draw. Counting each opponent's base draw, the cycle is nine opponent draws and eighteen cards. Claim, not fact: no stack has resolved this pairing.
Temple Bell's activation makes each player draw, so each opponent must pay {2} or hand you a Treasure. The mana route from the gift back to the {6}{W} bill. Claim, not fact.

Psychosis Crawler triggers on YOUR draws, not your opponents' - Temple Bell is one of the gift pieces that draws you a card too, which is what connects them. The only measured figure near this route is the seat's noncombat damage median of 0.0 over 120 games, and that seat also held three punishers this list has cut, so it is an upper bound on a route the current 99 has never had measured.

Scrawling Crawler triggers on OPPONENT draws, which is the other half of the pair and the half Howling Mine feeds. The declared 'Engine + punisher assembled' component prices the two-piece at 0.328 assembled, 0.196 by turn six - the deck's least reliable declared pairing.

CLAIM, and an unsettled one: the back face reduces generic cost, so a discount should let you choose a larger X on Stroke of Genius, Braingeyser, Prosperity, Skyscribing or Mathemagics. Whether that is how the cost is computed is in open_questions for resolve-stack; nothing on disk settles it.
via: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

lines.note: Sphinx's 'draw two cards' is two draw events, and the Archive replaces each draw after the first in a draw step - so an opponent's draw becomes four cards, not two. Claim: no stack has resolved it.
{6}{W} twice is fourteen mana across two turns, and goldfish mean_available_mana crosses 7 only between turn 8 (6.966) and turn 9 (7.612). This is the arrow the deck's whole mana base exists to draw.

DOWNGRADED from verified_by 002. The route is sound as oracle text - Mystical Tutor searches for "an instant or sorcery card" and Approach of the Second Sun is a Sorcery, both from cards.json - but stack 002 does not prove it: Mystical Tutor appears only in the scenario's graveyard and game_history, which are its PREMISE, no resolution step reasons about it, and the checker's own audit says the game_history sentence "is scenario flavor per orchestrator instruction, NOT A RULES CLAIM". What 002 proves is the destination - that a second cast from hand wins even though the card went back into the library - which is lines[9] and the wincon stage.

Stack 002 step 4: Swan Song held with {U} up counters the opponent's counter and Approach still resolves. The stack states the limit itself - Swan Song answers an enchantment, instant or sorcery SPELL, and cannot answer an activated or triggered ability.

The insurance package was added because the commander is fragile: the front face resolved in 68 of 120 games (0.567), 0.69 casts on the mean, and the BACK face - the one carrying the discount and the flash grant - appeared in only 35 (0.292). deck_versions v1.1.0's note prices the change against "a 45% removal rate" from 119 measured departures; that decomposition is not on disk in this deck's artifacts and is repeated here as the version's stated rationale, not as a figure I re-derived. The run predates the package, so its effect is unmeasured.
via: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

map_disagreements.why: The single most valuable disagreement in this deck. Six cards read the SAME input - an opponent drew a card, or cast a spell - and each states a different OUTPUT, so the map, which is built from card text, files them by what they produce. Smothering Tithe reads as ramp because it says Treasure. Heliod reads as a creature because his type line is one. Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Consecrated Sphinx and Faerie Mastermind read as draw. No card in the group says what the group is for, so this layer is invisible in card text and cannot be seen by a reader looking at the constellation.

26 cards across five cities - the map splits them by HOW they answer (counter text, destroy text, a body, a Treasure rider on An Offer You Can't Refuse) while the deck uses all of them for one job: buy turns until you can cast a seven-drop twice. Kefnet the Mindful lands in Card Flow because his activated ability draws, which is the least important thing he does here.

Pearl Medallion and Sapphire Medallion are cost reduction, not production, so the map puts them with the white spells and the X-creatures rather than with the rocks. In this deck they do the rocks' job - shave the bill on a colour-heavy curve - which is also how goldfish_targets counts them.

Nine of eleven cluster cleanly, which is unusual. The two strays are structural rather than semantic: Mikokoro is a land and its text is mostly a mana ability, and Enlightened Tutor is a search, so it sits with the other tutors regardless of what it fetches in this 99.

No disagreement, but the address is worth naming: Approach sits in Card Flow with the draw engine - the map read it on 'gain 7 life' and 'seventh from the top' - while Mystical Tutor and Long-Term Plans, the only two cards that find it, sit in Bodies. The deck's win and its route to the win have different addresses.

notes: STALENESS, and it applies to every Forge figure in this artifact: sim run giada-angels-vs-baylen-tokens-vs-abaddon-n120 carries heliod seat decklist_sha256 decc32b080fe - v1.0.0 - and the record's own note says the games were played on the launch .dck. The current list is 214af3084f80 (v1.2.1). Fourteen cards have changed since, including every card named in the protection stage's fort and insurance layers. The 120 games are evidence about the deck that PRODUCED the change, not about the deck that resulted from it. Every goldfish, benchmark and bracket figure quoted here does match the current sha.

The frame says why itself: Decanter of Endless Water "makes nobody draw" and was a member of the two draw groups, so "until it is removed from the two draw groups, the 0.935 / 0.854 / mean-turn-2.319 assembly figures count games where the only engine drawn was a mana rock, and the same overcount flows into Engine + punisher 0.334". At least six of the frame's figures differ from current goldfish_metrics.json: 0.935 / 0.854 / 2.319 against 0.920 / 0.828 / 2.461 for the table engine, 0.334 / 0.204 against 0.328 / 0.196 for engine-plus-punisher, and 0.679 against 0.495 for win-condition access. A membership fix changes what the old figures MEANT, so they are not comparable. This artifact uses goldfish_metrics.json throughout, via engine-facts.

Five stacks were retired to stacks/retired/ because they need cards this list no longer holds. Only 002 is cited here, and its board names Ancient Tomb, which the deck no longer runs; the ruling it establishes does not depend on that land.

ARCHETYPE, corrected in code since the previous revision: deck_audit now reads this deck as `control` (it had matched `combo` off the frame's sentence "there is no two-card combo"). Under control the SWEEPERS axis moves from at-target to UNDER - 2 copies, Day of Judgment and Supreme Verdict, against 5-7. Also under: mana-base (33 land copies against 37-39), colour-sources, and interaction-breadth (3 of 5 permanent classes answered; graveyard and land uncovered, and that detection is an oracle-text heuristic with counterspells excluded, so it is a floor).

The three goldfish_targets edits this artifact proposed at the previous revision are ALL APPLIED and were verified against goldfish_targets.json before this one was written: Walking Ballista is out of the win-condition any_of (three cards now), the punisher target is relabelled to name both Crawlers, and the flier-blocker label states Kefnet's seven-card condition. The section now carries one new proposal.

open_questions.question: Does Heliod, the Warped Eclipse's cost reduction let you choose a larger X on Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Mathemagics, Secure the Wastes, Walking Ballista, Hangarback Walker or Mikaeus, the Lunarch - and if so, is X chosen before or after the reduction applies?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The declared component 'An X-spell finisher drawn (the mana sink the discount pays for)' assembles 0.790 and its whole justification is this interaction. Nothing on disk tests it, and the conversion -> fuel line in this artifact is a claim resting on it.

open_questions.question: While Lightning Greaves is equipped to Heliod, can you still target him with Karametra's Blessing or Guardian of Faith's enters trigger, and is moving the Greaves off in response possible at instant speed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Greaves grants shroud, which stops your own targeting; equip is sorcery-speed. If two of the five commander-insurance slots are mutually exclusive with a third while equipped, the 0.680 assembly figure for that component overstates what the pilot can actually do in a removal window.

open_questions.question: Can the second Approach of the Second Sun be cast at an opponent's end step under Heliod's flash grant or Leyline of Anticipation, and is Fierce Guardianship's alternative cost live in that window when Heliod himself is the commander on the battlefield?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 002 resolves the sorcery-speed cast on your own turn. The end-step cast is a different and better window - it spends the table's responses first - and it needs either Leyline of Anticipation or Heliod's BACK face, which appeared in 0.292 of Forge games. The free-counter backup depends on the commander being on the battlefield in that window, which the record does not measure: resolved_rate 0.567 counts games where the front face resolved at least once, not games where he was still there.

open_questions.question: No declared target measures the deck's actual win: Approach in hand AND seven mana available on two separate turns. Can the harness express a mana condition, or must the gap be recorded rather than modelled?
open_questions.why_it_matters: "Win condition access" is a three-card any_of (Approach, Mystical Tutor, Long-Term Plans) and assembles 0.495, 0.677 with tutors, 0.361 by turn six - it measures DRAWING one of three cards. 20 of 27 measured wins are the second cast, and nothing in goldfish_targets.json prices whether the deck can pay for it: mean_available_mana crosses 7 only between turn 8 and turn 9.

open_questions.question: How many tutor and protection slots is a single 'you win the game' card worth in a four-player pod, and how should the one-window cast be timed against three potential responders?
open_questions.why_it_matters: strategic_frame.json's own gaps list says the strategy doc has NO section on alternate win conditions - the query returns 0.407 and nothing on topic. This deck's entire plan therefore has no home in the corpus, and the wincon stage has one card where threat-density asks for three to five.

open_questions.question: Can the goldfish measure the card side of this deck - Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind, Kefnet, Alhammarret's Archive, Teferi's Ageless Insight, Psychosis Crawler, Kwain and Loran are all in `draw_not_modelled` - so that a claim about whether mana or cards binds this deck has both arms measured?
open_questions.why_it_matters: meta.card_advantage reports 13 cards that draw against 2 modelled, and its own `why` says to read the two numbers together because the gap is a finding about the deck. Until the opponent-draw-triggered channel is modelled, the mana stage can only say mana is a MEASURED constraint, not that it is the binding one - and this deck's entire conversion stage is in the unmodelled list.

proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Drop Pearl Medallion and Sapphire Medallion from the any_of, or split the target into two need-groups - one for casting the front face, one for the flip - and keep the Medallions only in the first.
proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Heliod plus the mana to flip him ({3}{U/P} on top of {2}{W}{W})
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: The label names TWO costs and the group is scored as one. Pearl Medallion is "White spells you cast cost {1} less to cast" and Sapphire Medallion is the blue equivalent (oracle text, cards.json): both shave the {2}{W}{W} cast, and NEITHER can pay any part of "{3}{U/P}: Transform Heliod", because a cost reduction applies to spells and this is an activated ability. The other six members do pay it - {3} takes colourless, and {U/P} takes 2 life. The flip half is the half that matters now that it is separately measured: the back face appeared in 0.292 of Forge games against a 0.823 assembled_rate for this target, and two of its eight members cannot contribute to the event the label is about.

stages.label: WHAT PAYS FOR {6}{W} TWICE
stages.what_it_does:
32 of the deck's 33 land copies sit here, in 17 entries (Mikokoro is placed in ignition), plus eight rocks and cost-reducers. The bill this stage exists to pay is Approach's, twice: {6}{W} is seven mana, on two separate turns. goldfish mean_available_mana_by_turn crosses 7 between turn 8 (6.966) and turn 9 (7.612), and that is with the commander's discount switched OFF in the model.

Mana is the constraint this harness can MEASURE, which is not the same as the binding one: goldfish meta.card_advantage counts 13 cards that draw against 2 modelled, and the eleven it names include four of conversion's six. What is measured: benchmark missed_land_drop_rate 0.2532 with turn six the worst; land_drop_hit_rate 0.729 / 0.603 / 0.540 across turns four to six. mana_analysis.json (primary, same sha) gives 25 W and 26 U total sources against a Karsten 90%-on-curve figure of 36 each - and that file's own note says of these very numbers that "the target is a yardstick, not a possibility, in a 33-land deck". Lands-only on-curve probability 0.610 W / 0.639 U, and 0.580 / 0.610 with Skycloud Expanse set aside as the one gated source, whose coloured mode costs {1} extra.

Several cards here do a second job. Pearl Medallion and Sapphire Medallion reduce the cost of white and blue SPELLS rather than produce mana, which is why the map files them away from the other rocks - and why they cannot pay any part of the commander's flip; see proposed_goldfish_edits. Reliquary Tower, Decanter of Endless Water and Thought Vessel each carry "You have no maximum hand size", the clause Kefnet the Mindful and Psychosis Crawler both read. Eiganjo and Otawara are counted here for the mana they tap for, but each is also a channel answer discarded from hand, outside the deck's 21 answer cards.

evidence.note: 9 of 11 in Card Flow; Mikokoro in city-1 Mana, Enlightened Tutor in city-0 Bodies

deck-facts roles: Temple Bell, Faerie Mastermind, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Scrawling Crawler are the only draw:wheel cards; the taxonomy has no pattern at all for Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Dictate of Kruphix, Forced Fruition or Ghostly Prison, which is why the gift is invisible to roles

stages.label: THE GIFT - THE TABLE STARTS DRAWING
stages.what_it_does:
The first thing that has to happen, and the cheapest. EIGHT of the ten permanents here hand the WHOLE table cards - Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Kami of the Crescent Moon, Dictate of Kruphix, Temple Bell, Mikokoro, Kwain and The Second Doctor all say "each player". Two do not: Loran of the Third Path is "you and TARGET OPPONENT each draw a card", and Forced Fruition draws seven to the opponent who cast a spell and nobody else - which is also how it can kill you. The resource every later stage reads, a card an opponent drew this turn, does not exist until one of these resolves.

The rate belongs to the declared component, not to this stage. "Table draw engine online" assembles in 0.92 of goldfish games (0.97 with tutors), 0.828 by turn six, mean turn 2.461 - enumerated across all eleven declared targets, the highest assembled_rate (next 0.843) and the lowest mean turn (next 2.819). Its eleven members are these ten plus Scrawling Crawler, MINUS Enlightened Tutor. The substitution runs against this stage: Scrawling Crawler draws the table unaided, Enlightened Tutor only finds a card that does, at the cost of a second cast and a draw step - so the stage's own eleven would assemble somewhat below 0.92, and nobody has measured it.

Placements. Mikokoro is counted here, not in mana: "{2}, {T}: Each player draws a card" is what the deck wants from a colourless land. Scrawling Crawler is placed in output, because its drain is the louder half. Enlightened Tutor reaches five of these ten - Howling Mine, Font of Mythos, Temple Bell, Dictate of Kruphix and Forced Fruition, artifact or enchantment only - and cannot find Approach.

evidence.note: 6 of 10 in Card Flow (Alhammarret's Archive, Teferi's Ageless Insight, Stroke of Genius, Prosperity, Skyscribing, Mathemagics); the other 4 - Dig Through Time, Braingeyser, Mystical Tutor, Long-Term Plans - are in city-0 Bodies
deck-facts roles: only Drift of Phantasms and Long-Term Plans carry tutor:unrestricted, and Drift cannot reach Approach at mana value 7

stages.label: YOUR OWN CARD FLOW, AND THE ONLY ROUTE BACK
stages.what_it_does:
What keeps the deck running once the table is drawing: eight cards that turn mana into cards for you, plus the two tutors that can actually find the win.

Alhammarret's Archive and Teferi's Ageless Insight each read "if you would draw a card except the first one you draw in each of YOUR draw steps, draw two cards instead" - `your` is the load-bearing word in a deck whose gift fires in every player's draw step, and it means every draw of yours outside your own draw step is replaced. The declared component "Heliod down with an asymmetric card engine" (assembled 0.787, 0.581 by turn six) groups them with Rhystic Study and Consecrated Sphinx; they are split out here because they read YOUR draws, which is a different trigger and a different job. The five X-draw spells are the mana sink, and TWO of them - Prosperity and Skyscribing - draw the whole table; Braingeyser, Stroke of Genius and Mathemagics each target one player, and feed the same turn's discount only when aimed at an opponent. Dig Through Time delves, so its printed eight overstates what you pay.

ENUMERATED, because the role tag says otherwise: of the 99, only Mystical Tutor (instant or sorcery) and Long-Term Plans (any card, third from the top) can find Approach of the Second Sun. Enlightened Tutor is artifact-or-enchantment. Drift of Phantasms transmutes for mana value 3; Approach is 7. The declared "Win condition access" component is already down to those two plus Approach itself, and the three-card group assembles 0.495 (0.677 with tutors), 0.361 by turn six.

cards: Heliod, the Radiant Dawn // Heliod, the Warped Eclipse

evidence.note: 4 of 6 in Card Flow; Heliod in city-0 Bodies, Smothering Tithe in city-2 Ramp

deck-facts roles: Rhystic Study, Mystic Remora, Consecrated Sphinx, Faerie Mastermind and Smothering Tithe all carry draw:engine, but so do Arcane Denial, Psychosis Crawler, Scrawling Crawler and The Second Doctor - the role does not separate a converter from a draw spell

stages.label: THE ASYMMETRY LAYER - SIX CARDS, ONE TRIGGER
stages.what_it_does:
The engine proper. The gift is symmetric and therefore not card advantage; these six make it one-sided, reading the same event and paying it out in different currencies. Consecrated Sphinx: two cards on every opponent draw. Faerie Mastermind: one on each opponent's second draw each turn. Smothering Tithe: a Treasure per opponent draw unless they pay {2}. Rhystic Study and Mystic Remora bill casts, not draws.

THE COMMANDER IS TWO CARDS AND ONLY THE BACK ONE DOES THIS STAGE'S JOB. Heliod, the Warped Eclipse is "You may cast spells as though they had flash" and "Spells you cast cost {1} less to cast for each card your opponents have drawn this turn"; the front face is a {2}{W}{W} body with an enchantment-recursion ETB and "{3}{U/P}: Transform Heliod. Activate only as a sorcery". Two events, and the run prices both: he RESOLVED in 68 of 120 games (0.567 [0.477, 0.652]) and TRANSFORMED in 35 (0.292 [0.218, 0.378]). The multiplier this stage is named for was live in 35 games, not 68; in 85 of 120 it never appeared and the deck still took its 27 wins, 20 with Approach. Multiplier, then, not ignition - the gift assembles at 0.92, mean player-turn 2.461, without waiting on the flip.

Two cautions. Forge turns advance once per PLAYER turn (the parser's limit: "turn 24 of a four-handed game is round 6"), so the median first flip at global turn 34 is not comparable to a goldfish player turn. And the seat is sha decc32b080fe, v1.0.0: v1.1.0 bought five insurance cards against this fragility (lines[10]) and nothing re-measured it. `model-coverage` gives Heliod one channel, `bodies`, so every goldfish mana figure here has the discount OFF.

No `fodder` stage: nothing here is converted by being spent. The resource the engine eats is manufactured on the opponents' side of the table.

evidence.note: 4 of 6 in Bodies; both Crawlers in city-3 Card Flow
deck-facts roles: Psychosis Crawler and Scrawling Crawler are the only two cards in the 99 carrying wincon:drain

stages.label: WHAT IT PRODUCES, AND HOW LITTLE
stages.what_it_does:
Six cards, and the measured verdict on them is the most useful line in this model. Psychosis Crawler drains each opponent 1 on every card YOU draw and has power and toughness equal to your hand size. FOUR cards in the 99 lift the discard step and one is symmetric: Reliquary Tower, Decanter of Endless Water and Thought Vessel read "YOU have no maximum hand size"; The Second Doctor reads "PLAYERS have no maximum hand size", so three opponents drawing extra off the gift also keep it all - a cost the ignition stage does not price. Scrawling Crawler drains an opponent per draw and hands the whole table an upkeep card, so it is half an ignition piece. Four X-cards leave a permanent behind: Secure the Wastes, Walking Ballista, Hangarback Walker (which dies into flying Thopters) and Mikaeus, the Lunarch.

Read the medians. Over 120 Forge games heliod dealt combat damage to players with mean 4.11 and MEDIAN 0.5; commander damage reached 21 in zero games; and heliod was credited with 7 eliminations across the whole run (baylen-tokens 4, abaddon 2, giada-angels 1). This is a value and blocking layer, not a clock. The pilot cut Iron Maiden, Viseling and Ebony Owl Netsuke on exactly that evidence - 81 castings across the 120 games (26 + 33 + 22, counted in the run's own logs) for a MEDIAN of zero noncombat damage. The run's noncombat MEAN of 1.68 is deliberately not used here: engine-critic re-derived the same logs and got several times that from those three cards alone, an open attribution question about the parser. The median is unaffected either way - and those three were IN the measured list and are NOT in this one, so the current 99's noncombat output is unmeasured. What remains of the axis is the declared two-card component: 0.366 assembled, 0.256 by turn six.

stages.label: THE 26 CARDS THAT BUY THE TURNS
stages.what_it_does:
The largest stage by a distance, 26 of 85 entries, and its job is to survive to a seven-drop you must cast twice. Four layers, each with its own figure.

COUNTERS (8, two of them free - Force of Negation and Fierce Guardianship). "Free or cheap interaction held" assembles 0.843, 0.707 by turn six, but interaction_castable is 0.626 at turn six against 0.927 in hand: holding it and paying for it are different problems.

REMOVAL (7), of which only Day of Judgment and Supreme Verdict are sweepers - two against a control target of 5-7, which deck_audit reads as UNDER.

THE FORT (6): Propaganda, Ghostly Prison and Archangel of Tithes tax attackers - 0.487 assembled, 0.355 by turn six, the least reliable of the four defensive components. Angelic Wall, Drift of Phantasms, Kefnet and Archangel are this stage's share of the six-card flier-blocker component (Sphinx and Faerie Mastermind are the other two, in conversion), 0.750 assembled. Kefnet cannot block below seven cards in hand.

COMMANDER INSURANCE (5): Lightning Greaves, Guardian of Faith, Karametra's Blessing, Teferi's Protection, and Leyline of Anticipation, which duplicates the flash grant without him. 0.680 assembled, 0.526 by turn six.

TWO layers, TWO measurements. The insurance is v1.1.0, taken on "a 45% removal rate" from "the decomposition of 119 measured departures". The fort is v1.2.0, taken on 39 of 53: `eliminated_by` attributes 39 of heliod's 53 ATTRIBUTED eliminations to giada-angels, whose every threat flies. The denominator matters - heliod was eliminated in 74 of 120 games and `eliminated_how` records only {damage: 53}, so 21 deaths have no attributed killer and are unknown, not non-damage. Combat damage taken: mean 36.08, median 24.0, on the v1.0.0 seat that predates both layers.

Approach sits in Card Flow with the draw engine, not with the tutors that find it

evidence.id: Approach of the Second Sun + Mystical Tutor
evidence.note: the single contained Commander Spellbook line, bracket 3, produces 'Win the game'; it is a candidate, and stack 002 is what makes this one a fact

stages.label: ONE CARD
stages.what_it_does:
Approach of the Second Sun, cast twice from hand. The first cast gains 7 life and puts the card seventh from the top; the second wins outright. It is 20 of the deck's 27 wins over 120 Forge games - the run record's own tally of won_by "effect of 'Approach of the Second Sun'". The other 7 read "all opponents have lost": attrition, which has no card of its own, and which is why this stage names exactly one. So the label is true of the deck's AGENCY and not of its win column - roughly a quarter of the wins did not need the card. Mean finishing position 2.319 over 94 ranked games (16 firsts, 43 seconds, 24 thirds, 11 fourths); win rate 0.252, CI95 [0.180, 0.342] over the run's 107 decided games, against a four-seat null of 0.250 - dead parity. All of it is the v1.0.0 seat, sha decc32b080fe.

Verified stack 002 settles the whole skill. The win is checked during Approach's resolution as a spell effect, not a state-based action, so the only window to stop it is while Approach is on the stack before all players pass priority; once resolution begins nobody has priority again. The first casting still counts although the card was shuffled back into the library, because the condition tracks a casting event in game history rather than a card object. Two caveats the stack states itself: Swan Song answers a spell only, not an activated or triggered ability; and 002's board names Ancient Tomb, which this list no longer runs - the ruling does not depend on it.

This is a ONE-finisher deck, and the pilot's standing constraint against two-card infinites rules out the usual second route. bracket_report.json reads two_card_infinites: 0, with the deck's floor at 4 on 8 Game Changers.

thesis: Heliod manufactures a resource nobody at the table prices - cards in your opponents' hands - converts it into a cost discount, one-sided draw, Treasure and life loss, and spends the turns that buys casting Approach of the Second Sun twice.
